newsitem.title: UK: Shell details 1997 North Sea maintainence plans.
newsitem.headline: Shell details 1997 North Sea maintainence plans.

text.p: Shell UK Exploration and Production (Shell Expro) announced on Wednesday its maintenance plans for work at its North Sea platforms, showing a similar level of activity as last year.

The main shutdown will be at the 55,000 barrels per day (bpd) Brent Delta platform which will close on April 1 and will not resume oil production until early in the final quarter of the year, Shell Expro said.
Brent Delta gas exports will not resume until two months after oil flows restart.
The lengthy Delta shutdown is part of Shell Expro's $1.3 billion refurbishment. Last year, the 69,000 bpd Brent Charlie platform was shut for about the same length of time.
The 57,000-bpd Brent Alpha platform is due to shut for maintenance May 1-14 and the 70,000 bpd Brent Bravo platform will close June 1-7.
Shell Expro is a joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Exxon.
